title: Iran Talks Ride a Fraying Truce, Abu Dhabi Next, Mississippi Waits on Affidavits
bluf: Iran is still the center of gravity: Qatar says Washington and Tehran are each reviewing a mediators' draft, Tehran offers to reopen Hormuz within two days of a deal and leave nuclear issues for later, while a reported US strike on Qeshm Island and continued tanker hits show the truce fraying. Ukraine, Russia and the US meet in Abu Dhabi November 10 to 11 for the first formal round since February; the Kremlin says preparing for talks does not limit its operations. Mississippi's Senate race remains uncalled, with Scott Colom 43 votes ahead in the latest count and an estimated 10,000 to 15,000 affidavit ballots still to process. In Israel, the opposition has rallied behind Gadi Eisenkot and Isaac Herzog must name someone to form a government by November 11. Taiwan logged its busiest day of Chinese military flights this year as the PLA's drill season opens.

corrections.text: Edition 002 said a former FBI agent named Andrew Reyes was charged on November 5. This run could not find any source for that charge or that name. Treat that item as unverified; it has been dropped until a court record or DOJ release confirms it.
Edition 002 gave Scott Colom's Mississippi lead as about 138 votes. The latest count found today (Mississippi Free Press) puts it at 43 votes.

worldConditions.overall: The Iran war and the shipping fight in Hormuz remain the main driver of global risk, with diplomacy and strikes running at the same time. A second front of pressure is building around Taiwan as the PLA's drill season starts. In the US, the transition to a Democratic Congress is orderly but one Senate seat is still in play.
worldConditions.postureBasis: Active US and Iranian kinetic exchanges near a global chokepoint, a major power naval surge near Taiwan, and no ceasefire in Ukraine.

items.headline: Mississippi Senate seat comes down to affidavit ballots
items.summary: Democrat Scott Colom led Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by 43 votes in the latest count reported by the Mississippi Free Press, out of nearly 1 million cast. Colom's campaign estimated 10,000 to 15,000 affidavit ballots (the provisional ballots voters cast when their registration is in question) were still outstanding. Hyde-Smith's campaign says it is confident she wins once every legally cast ballot is counted; Colom has sent lawyers to watch county officials. Mississippi has no recount law, so any fight would be over which ballots count, in court.
items.source: Mississippi Today; Mississippi Free Press; Democracy Docket
items.assessment: We assess the outcome is a roughly even chance either way until affidavit tallies are reported; the first statewide indication is unlikely before next week, per voter advocates quoted by CNN.

items.headline: Why so many affidavit ballots: 230,000 voters flagged inactive
items.summary: Secretary of State Michael Watson flagged about 230,000 registrations as inactive this cycle, using a commercial credit data program for the first time to clean the rolls. Those voters could still vote, but only by affidavit ballot. Supporters of the cleanup say accurate rolls protect elections; critics say it pushed eligible voters into a slower, contestable process. Harrison County, on the Coast, says it will not count affidavits until November 10.
items.source: Democracy Docket; CNN via WTTW; Mississippi Free Press

items.headline: Mississippi Democrats challenge DeSoto County precinct problems
items.summary: On election night the state Democratic Party went to court over DeSoto County precincts it says opened late, had very long waits and ran short of regular and affidavit ballots. County officials' response was not collected this run.

items.headline: Montana: Republican Kurt Alme wins Senate seat
items.summary: AP called Montana's Senate race for Republican Kurt Alme on Wednesday. It is one of the few Republican pickups or holds in a cycle Democrats otherwise dominated.

items.headline: Michigan: Abdul El-Sayed wins open Senate seat
items.summary: Progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's Senate race over Republican Mike Rogers, according to Gray TV reporting. Rogers had made election integrity claims during the campaign that fact checkers disputed.

alsoNoted.headline: FBI Houston says social posts about an election 'raid' finding fake ballots are untrue
Trump's defamation suit against the Wall Street Journal dismissed

items.headline: Qatar: both sides are reviewing a mediators' draft
items.summary: Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari said the US and Iran are each reviewing proposals put forward by the mediators, that differences remain and talks continue. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has floated reopening the Strait of Hormuz within two days of a deal and leaving nuclear issues to a second phase. Secretary of State Marco Rubio says talks have never stopped and Washington is open to a diplomatic solution.
items.source: Express Tribune (Al Arabiya); Iran International; Al Jazeera
items.assessment: Washington's stated position is that the nuclear stockpile comes first; Tehran's plan puts it last. Until one side moves on sequencing, we assess a framework remains unlikely before year end (moderate confidence).

items.headline: US strikes Qeshm Island; IRGC says it downed two US drones
items.summary: Drop Site News reported a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz, on November 3, and an IRGC claim that it captured two US surveillance drones over the island. US officials had not publicly detailed the strike in sources collected this run.
items.assessment: If confirmed, this is the first US strike inside Iran since the midterms window that officials had flagged.

items.headline: Tanker strikes: Iran claims many, UKMTO confirms few
items.summary: The IRGC Navy keeps reporting multiple tankers hit each day. The British military's UKMTO center confirmed only one strike late on November 3: the Barbados flagged tanker Grit, which trade sources describe as part of the shadow fleet and Chinese owned since June. Iran's Tasnim agency said three tankers hit mines after entering unauthorized lanes with transponders off.

items.headline: Treasury: no new oil loaded at Iran's terminals since August 25
items.summary: A US Treasury report shared with Axios found no new crude loaded onto tankers at Iran's terminals since August 25 and called Iran's economy crippled, though not near collapse. The White House frames this as pressure working; Iranian officials say it will not force them to give up the stockpile first.

items.headline: Inside Iran: student sit in, execution fears, and a bomb debate in the open
items.summary: Students at the University of Tehran held a sit in on November 3, chanting against both war and bloodshed. Iran International reports three protesters face imminent execution and that open debate about building a nuclear weapon is gaining ground on official platforms. Iran International is an opposition leaning outlet based in London; Tehran calls it hostile media.

items.headline: Araghchi: any talks would cover only the nuclear issue
items.summary: Iran's official news agency IRNA quoted Araghchi on November 4 saying any negotiations with the United States would focus solely on the nuclear file, which sits awkwardly with his own two phase plan that defers it. Tehran has not explained the difference.

items.headline: Opposition lines up behind Eisenkot; Herzog must name someone by November 11
items.summary: Opposition leaders including Naftali Bennett, Yair Lapid, Avigdor Liberman and Yair Golan agreed to recommend Gadi Eisenkot to President Isaac Herzog and promised a national emergency government. Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats and Eisenkot's 48; with Arab led parties the anti Netanyahu side reaches 67, but several opposition leaders have said they will not govern with them. Netanyahu says he wants a broad national government. The Knesset is sworn in November 10; the nominee then gets 28 days, plus a possible 14.
items.assessment: We assess Eisenkot is likely to get the first mandate (moderate confidence), but a stable coalition without the Arab parties or Likud is unlikely; a unity government or a new election stay live options.

items.headline: Rafah crossing blocked to aid and commercial goods
items.summary: A senior Palestinian source involved in negotiations told Drop Site News that the Rafah crossing was blocking humanitarian aid, commercial goods, food, fuel and cooking gas from entering Gaza by the Egyptian route. Israeli and Egyptian explanations were not collected this run.

alsoNoted.headline: Thousands rallied in Tel Aviv urging Eisenkot to deal with Arab parties
Xinhua's framing: opposition pledges swift move to replace Netanyahu

items.headline: Abu Dhabi talks November 10 to 11: what is on the table
items.summary: Steve Witkoff says the US will mediate working level talks covering postwar security, de escalation, humanitarian steps and ending the war. Reporting points to an energy and maritime ceasefire, prisoner exchanges and the return of Ukrainian children taken to Russia. It is the fourth formal round this year and the first since February, when the Iran war froze the process. Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to lead the US side.
items.source: Khaleej Times; Latin Times; Kyiv Post
items.assessment: We assess a limited deal (prisoners, an energy strike pause) is likely; a full ceasefire from this round is unlikely, since the Kremlin ties peace to territory.

items.headline: Kremlin: preparing talks does not mean limiting operations
items.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said preparing for the talks implies no commitment to limit military operations, and that every Ukrainian strike would get what he called a fully justified response. Aide Yury Ushakov called the meeting decisive and said Moscow will not invite Europeans.

items.headline: Merz: Russia has yet to engage seriously; Europe not at the table
items.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, hosting Volodymyr Zelensky in Berlin, said Russia has not seriously engaged on a ceasefire. European governments want a seat but are unlikely to be in Abu Dhabi. Zelensky hopes the talks open the way to a leaders meeting with Putin.

items.headline: Taiwan reports year's highest single day of PLA air activity and 100 plus ships
items.summary: Taiwan's defense ministry counted 49 PLA aircraft sorties in the 24 hours to 6am November 3, the highest one day total this year, falling to 22 the next day. Security chief Joseph Wu said more than 100 Chinese navy and coast guard ships were spread across the western Pacific, including the Liaoning carrier group drilling in the Philippine Sea. Taiwan has warned that November and December are the PLA's peak drill season.
items.assessment: Consistent with our forecast that a named encirclement drill this year is likely; this is pressure signaling, not mobilization for invasion (moderate confidence).

items.headline: Law 186 takes effect Monday: what actually changes
items.summary: Law 186, published November 2 in the Official Gazette, takes effect November 9 and cuts Cuba's central state bodies from 27 to 21: 20 ministries plus the Central Bank. It merges portfolios, for example a new Ministry of Environment, Habitat and Water Resources covering housing, water and the land registry, and ends a standalone Internal Commerce ministry. Ministers have 30 days to file work schedules and up to a year to finish mergers. The text sets no job cut numbers and no wage changes, and a transitional provision addresses the ration book.
items.source: Directorio Cubano; The Rio Times; CubaHeadlines
items.assessment: The government says the aim is efficiency; critics in independent Cuban media say it reshuffles the same system. Both claims will be testable once organization charts appear.

items.headline: Fridge attacks: second wave hit seven countries; still no attribution
items.summary: Overnight into November 2, attackers switched supermarket refrigeration controllers into defrost mode in Belgium, the Netherlands, Sweden, Luxembourg, Ireland, Estonia and beyond, heating some units to 50°C. It followed a first wave in France on October 11 and 12. France's cyber agency ties both to internet exposed Danfoss and Copeland/Dixell controllers, many no longer updated. Belgian federal prosecutors opened a case. No government or group has named a culprit.
items.assessment: Researchers think an automated script hit a scanned target list, which fits a criminal or hacktivist actor as well as a state. We hold attribution at unassessed (low confidence).

conspiracies.claim: The FBI raided a Houston office on November 2 and found fraudulent ballots.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Social media posts during election week
conspiracies.whyBelieved: Distrust of election administration after 2020, and real disputes this week over affidavit ballots and voter rolls make a raid story feel plausible.
conspiracies.caseFor: Believers point to real, documented fights over ballots this week (Mississippi affidavits, DeSoto County complaints) and to past federal election fraud prosecutions as proof such raids happen.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: FBI Houston publicly said the information is false and that no election related operation took place. No court filing, warrant or local report of a raid has surfaced.
conspiracies.unknowns: Who first posted the claim and whether it was a misread of an unrelated operation.
conspiracies.watch: Whether the claim attaches to the Mississippi count.
conspiracies.forumChatter: Described in an FBI statement reported by KTAR; forum level spread not measured by researchers in sources collected.

conspiracies.claim: Trump posted that Republicans already won all 50 states and counting should stop.
conspiracies.origin: A Facebook page that labels itself satire, per MEAWW's fact check
conspiracies.whyBelieved: It fits Trump's real past statements questioning vote counts in 2020, so readers on both sides found it believable.
conspiracies.caseFor: Trump has repeatedly disputed counts before, and screenshots of his real posts circulate the same way.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: Searches of his Truth Social account and archives found no such post, and the image traces to a parody page.
conspiracies.watch: Reuse if the Mississippi count drags on.
conspiracies.audience: Cross partisan (shared by critics as real, and by supporters as a joke)
conspiracies.forumChatter: Not described by researchers in sources collected.

conspiracies.claim: Mississippi's voter roll cleanup was designed to suppress Democratic and Black voters.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Left leaning social accounts and voting rights commentary
conspiracies.origin: Reaction to the affidavit ballot surge
conspiracies.whyBelieved: About 230,000 registrations were flagged inactive with commercial credit data used for the first time, right before an unexpectedly close race, in a state with a long documented history of voter suppression.
conspiracies.caseFor: The scale and timing are real and documented; the affected voters must now go through a slower, challengeable process; the race margin is smaller than the number of affidavit ballots.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: Federal law requires states to maintain their rolls, inactive voters were still allowed to vote, and no data published so far shows who was flagged by race or party.
conspiracies.unknowns: The demographic breakdown of flagged voters and how many affidavits will be accepted.
conspiracies.watch: County acceptance rates and any lawsuit.
conspiracies.forumChatter: Not described by researchers in sources collected.

conspiracies.claim: Russia is behind the European supermarket fridge attacks.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: European commentary and pro Ukraine accounts
conspiracies.origin: Pattern matching with the wider hybrid campaign against Europe
conspiracies.whyBelieved: The attacks are coordinated, overnight and cross border, and Europe has seen sabotage and hoax threats tied to Russia this year.
conspiracies.caseFor: Simultaneous triggering across countries suggests planning; critical infrastructure disruption fits a known Russian playbook; the EU called the attacks deliberate.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: No government has attributed the attacks. Researchers say an automated script hitting known flaws and default passwords on old, exposed devices could be run by criminals or hacktivists.
conspiracies.unknowns: Whether any ransom, claim or forensic link exists.
conspiracies.forumChatter: Not described by researchers in sources collected.

conspiracies.claim: A scientist predicted the world ends on Friday, November 13, 2026.
conspiracies.origin: A real 1960 Science paper on population growth
conspiracies.whyBelieved: It traces to a real peer reviewed paper that named the date.
conspiracies.caseFor: The paper exists and did name the date.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: The authors used it as a warning about growth trends; population growth later slowed, departing from the model.
conspiracies.watch: Mainstream explainers in the final week.
conspiracies.forumChatter: Not described by researchers in sources collected.
